data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003 argues that 'management debt' from coordinating across independent operators makes decentralized networks less resilient because drift creates cascading failures from upstream dependency updates. But it relies on an asserted causal chain — that independent operator drift will lead to correlated failures — while offering no evidence criterion to distinguish those failures from genuinely independent ones, which is the explicit question. More critically, SRC_003's own mechanism defeats its claim: if a 'single upstream dependency update triggers a cascading failure across the decentralized network,' that is a shared-cause (common-dependency) failure, not a failure intrinsic to the network's topology. A large unified service depending on the same upstream component would fail identically and simultaneously across all its redundant nodes. SRC_003 provides no evidence that the unified service avoids this common-cause exposure (e.g., through dependency isolation or multi-vendor diversity), so it has not shown that the large service is more resilient — it has merely relocated the shared cause from operator drift to a shared dependency, which the problem specifically asks us to detect.
